text: Warrior women is a mythic motif in the old Celtic world. Several goddesses made war their craft. British Andraste and Irish Badb follow this pattern. Gaulish Cathubodua also had war in her charge. Some heroines fought as warriors themselves. The queen Medb of Connacht led her armed hosts. Scáthach trained heroes from her home on the Isle of Skye, among them Cúchulainn. Her child or double Aífe trained beside heroes and bore their offspring. The record keeps a few warrior queens. Boudicca and Cartimandua led their tribes in battle. Most scholars still judge that Celtic women rarely joined the fight.
